questions.knowledge_point: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix
questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}({A}^{T})$ for every matrix $A?$

- $\text{Col}(A)$
- $\text{Null}(A)$
- $\text{Col}({A}^{T})$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Null}({A}^{T})$ is the left null space of $A.$ This consists of vectors that, when pre-multiplied by ${A}^{T},$ result in the zero-vector $0.$

When pre-multiplying a vector by ${A}^{T},$ we actually multiply each row of ${A}^{T}$, that is, each column of $A$, by that vector. So, $\text{Null}({A}^{T})$ must be orthogonal to the column space of $A,$ which is $\text{Col}(A).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/de22dd5b352e1d5be48f4b6ed3b2a4657ae623c1bd288d3464559758ea334af7.png)

questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ for every matrix $B?$

- $\text{Col}(B)$
- $\text{Null}({B}^{T})$
- $\text{Null}(B)$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ is the row space of $B.$ This consists of all linear combinations of the rows of $B.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of $B,$ it must be orthogonal to each row of $B.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by $B,$ we actually multiply each row of $B$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ must be orthogonal to the null space of $B,$ which is $\text{Null}(B).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(XY)$ for all compatible matrices $X$ and $Y?$

- $\text{Null}({Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T})$
- $\text{Col}(XY)$
- $\text{Col}({Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T})$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Null}(XY)$ contains all vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $XY,$ result in the zero-vector $0.$ 

When pre-multiplying a vector by $XY,$ we actually multiply each row of $XY$ by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(XY)$ must be orthogonal to the row space of $XY,$ which is $\text{Col}((XY)^{T})=\text{Col}({Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of ${B}^{T},$ it must be orthogonal to each row of ${B}^{T}.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by ${B}^{T},$ we actually multiply each row of ${B}^{T}$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}(B)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $B,$ which is $\text{Null}({B}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action
questions.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m\times n$ matrices. What is the image of $\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ under the action of $A+B?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $A+B$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A+B:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ (a+b)_{1} & (a+b)_{2} & ⋯ & (a+b)_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A+B}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A+B$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B),$ the column space of $A+B.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(A+B)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((A+B)^{T})=\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/02a739d8888f2b46b81075218693e6b2cc87e3c5b81b522abfc9246dcd7c870d.png)

questions.problem: Let $A$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $A$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & ⋯ & {a}_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A$ must be $\text{Col}(A),$ the column space of $A.$

questions.problem: Let $A$ be a $4\times 6$ matrix. What is the image of ${R}^{4}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${A}^{T}$ is a $6\times 4$ matrix.

Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ by ${A}^{T}$ gives a linear combination of the columns of ${A}^{T}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {a}_{1}^{T} & {a}_{2}^{T} & {a}_{3}^{T} & {a}_{4}^{T} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{T}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{3}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{4}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{4}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}$ must be $\text{Col}({A}^{T}),$ the row space of $A.$

questions.problem: Let $B$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ under the action of $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $B$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $B:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & ⋯ & {b}_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{B}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {b}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {b}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {b}_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $B$ must be $\text{Col}(B),$ the column space of $B.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(B)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(B).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

In our case, we are given that $m=7,$ $n=5,$ and $r=4.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{dim}(\text{Null}({A}^{T})) & =m-r=7-4=3.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Consider a $8 \times 6$ matrix $A.$ If $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A)) = 3,$ then find $\text{dim}(\text{Col}(A^T)).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/889b83fadd26b377c4dd34143c9b16541630c04e90de3d9b005e7147ead75ad5.png)

In our case, we are given that $m=8,$ $n=6,$ and $n-r=3.$ 

Substituting $n=6$ into $n-r=3,$ we can find the rank of $A{:}$

$$
6 - r = 3 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
r = 3
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{dim}(\text{Col}({A}^{T})) & =r=3.\end{aligned}
$$
